stem: The compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$, which gives only one monobromo derivative and takes up four moles of hydrogen per mole for complete hydrogenation has _______ $\pi$ electrons.

steps.text: $\ce{C6H6}$ has 4 degrees of unsaturation. Taking up four moles of $\ce{H2}$ for complete hydrogenation (to $\ce{C6H14}$) means all four are $\pi$ bonds, with no ring.
Four $\pi$ bonds contain $4\times2=8$ $\pi$ electrons. (Benzene, which absorbs three moles of $\ce{H2}$, does not fit.)

pitfalls: Answering 6 as for benzene.
solution.final_check: 8, matches the official NTA final key.
